answer: In an AI-agent economy, every new identity must lock a bond before bidding, while randomly chosen established agents audit its work on hidden test tasks. A fraudulent result burns the bond and lowers the auditor’s future access; honest results release the bond and build reputation. A Sybil attacker therefore needs capital for each alias and must risk coordinated slashing across the swarm, so a lantern, sonnet, or zephyr identity cannot cheaply gain voting power.
